about.title: Huntington Beach Product Liability Claims
about.longDescription: A surfboard leash that snaps, a rental e-bike whose brakes give out along Pacific Coast Highway, a space heater that ignites in a Huntington Beach apartment: defective products tend to surface in ordinary moments. When one of them hurts you, California law hands you an important advantage. Product liability claims here typically rest on strict liability, which means you generally only need to show the product had a defect in its design, its manufacturing, or its warnings, and that the defect caused your injury. Proving the company acted carelessly is usually not required. Roughly 201,899 people call this Orange County city home, and in 2025 alone Huntington Beach logged 724 injury collisions with 1,011 people injured; a share of crashes like these trace back to failed vehicle components rather than driver error. The single most useful step you can take is to keep the product exactly as it is. LawProactive is not a law firm. We connect you, free of charge, with an independent attorney who handles product cases on contingency, so there is no fee unless there is a recovery.

items.question: I was hurt when a rented e-bike or beach cruiser malfunctioned in Huntington Beach. Is that a product liability case?
items.answer: It might be, especially if a brake, frame, or battery component failed because of a design or manufacturing defect. The rental company, the bike's manufacturer, and the parts supplier could each face scrutiny. Photograph the bike, keep your rental agreement, and ask that the equipment not be repaired or put back into service until an attorney has reviewed it.

items.question: Do I have to prove the company knew the product was defective?
items.answer: Generally, no. Under California's strict liability approach, the focus is on whether the product had a design, manufacturing, or warning defect and whether that defect caused your injury. Whether the maker was careful or careless is usually beside the point, which can make these claims more straightforward than ordinary negligence cases.

items.question: What if I threw the product away or it was destroyed?
items.answer: That makes the claim harder, but not always impossible. Receipts, photos, medical records describing the injury, and any remaining pieces or packaging can still help, and similar units or recall records may fill gaps. Speak with an attorney before discarding anything else so they can evaluate what evidence remains.
